bounded_residuals.bounded_handling: Add release-hash/inode-based recovery reconciliation or require and document manual reconciliation before retry.
bounded_residuals.evidence: A crash after rename but before receipt append/save leaves the move unrecorded. The target directory then exists, so a rerun fails the unique-target precondition and cannot reconcile.
bounded_residuals.impact: Moved content remains in Trash, but the operation is partially unreceipted and not restartable.

findings.closure: Keep source extractions preserve-only unless the exact extracted tree is content-bound to a retained archive/distribution and its owner confirms it has no remaining consumer; restrict released categories to the authorized set.
findings.evidence: The selection has 23 source_archive_extraction items. The mover accepts any released item whose per-item status is changed to RELEASED_TO_TRASH; no category allowlist exists. Source extraction refs are checked only for existence and containment, not content equality/unchanged status or consumer closure. The release authorization string names repeatable test directories and used environments, not source extractions.
findings.impact: An editable extraction containing unique changes or still needed by a consumer can be moved to Trash based only on an adjacent archive/distribution existing.

findings.closure: Bind the final selection to the current inventory bytes; derive and require the exact admitted C roots from that inventory (or an immutable root-owned manifest), and reject any candidate/owner outside that set.
findings.evidence: The current script checks canonical paths, and iterates release-supplied roots/topics, but never loads selection.source_inventory_path or verifies its SHA against selection.source_inventory_sha256. It never requires release.exact_admitted_C_roots to equal the inventory’s 14-root set. Its additional path-prefix check admits any path under .codex/worktrees.
findings.impact: A malformed or re-authored final selection/release can broaden cleanup to another worktree while satisfying the caller-supplied owner set and path-prefix checks.

findings.closure: Compile the release input root-only from the expected complete topic/audit set after branch/HEAD/cleanliness checks; bind all required handoff/output refs to those frozen heads and verify exact set completeness.
findings.evidence: The committed-work/audit-complete predicates are release JSON booleans. Git references are SHA/byte checked but only required to be nonempty; frozen_topics has no required nonempty or exact topic set and its references are not tied to all required deciding outputs/useful changes or reachable from each frozen HEAD.
findings.impact: A partial or unrelated set can satisfy the code while release metadata declares all audits and deciding outputs complete.

findings.closure: Confine output_path to a new unique receipt below the exact cleanup directory, reject overlap and symlink ancestry, create exclusively, and use safe same-directory receipt updates.
findings.evidence: output_path is an arbitrary command-line path, and save() overwrites it via write_text without checking existence, symlink ancestors, containment under cleanup scratch, or overlap with a candidate/preservation path.
findings.impact: A caller path mistake can truncate a probe, receipt, or other file before any candidate move.

findings.closure: lstat and reject symlink refs; bind file hashes/byte counts or directory identity from the frozen inventory; globally prove no preserve ref is inside any released candidate path.
findings.evidence: Path.exists() follows symlinks and verifies only existence, both before and after rename. The mover does not bind reference lstat identity/content or reject a reference that is itself another released candidate.
findings.impact: A symlink/replacement can produce a false preserved-ref receipt; references could disappear later in the same batch if they belong to another released candidate.

findings.closure: Include lstat identity in the frozen final selection and require it to match the initial and immediate pre-rename lstat; otherwise hold the candidate.
findings.evidence: The immediate pre-rename inode comparison correctly detects replacement after the initial preflight, but selection items do not carry device/inode, and the initial preflight is not compared with the lstat identity recorded when the final selection was compiled.
findings.impact: A same-owner ignored directory can replace a selected path between selection and mover startup and be moved as if it were the selected object.
